focus: ompug diagram-codebase: Mermaid linter, sanitizer, deterministic ID builder
noveltyJustification: Ten findings are new and two corroborate iteration 1 with implemented severity; (10 + 1) / 12 = 0.917.
keyQuestions: Which pre-write model check, rule set or validator does each corpus skill define before a FigJam write, and which of those rules are machine-enforced rather than advisory?

Which write route does each corpus skill use (hosted MCP `generate_diagram`, `use_figma` plugin API, console bridge, direct `fj`-style node script), and what read-back or verification follows the write?

Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?
ruledOut: Adopting the full lint rule set verbatim into flow_check.py

label: ompug lint.py is a machine port of the official generate_diagram rules; any error blocks the write, making it the corpus's only other executable pre-write gate beside flow_check.py.
ompug's reserved-ID list extends the official three words with the Mermaid keywords style, class, classdef, click, default, flowchart, direction and linkstyle, all as errors.
Underscored node and subgraph IDs are errors because they break Figma edge routing, while non-camelCase is only a warning, a usable severity split for Flow Mode.
ompug's direction check accepts LR/TD/TB/RL/BT and only demands LR for architecture diagrams, machine-enforced counterevidence to Flow Mode's TD-only rule.
ompug catches emoji, literal newline escapes, HTML tags, control and invisible characters, unbalanced quotes and backticks, several of which Flow Mode does not check.
ompug both rejects and repairs: normalize_text strips emoji, HTML, invisible/control characters and backticks from generated labels, whereas Flow Mode only rejects.
ompug derives deterministic camelCase IDs and its allocator appends a suffix to reserved words, making reserved-ID collisions impossible rather than merely detectable.
id_map exposes spec-id to Mermaid-id so the driver can verify what was drawn; Flow Mode's provenance table has no model-id to board-node mapping.
Labels are capped at 80 characters with ellipsis and IDs at 32 with a short hash, while Flow Mode has a one-line rule but no length cap.
ompug's optional real-parser check reports unavailable as not run and never as passed, a truthfulness state Flow Mode's hand-written extractor lacks.
ompug splits oversized diagrams into parts and requires omitted content to be named in notes, never dropped silently; Flow Mode splits but does not require naming omissions.
ompug skips unsupported diagram types with a reason rather than faking them, the same honesty rule Flow Mode applies to unreachable routes but one level earlier.

direction: Adopting the full lint rule set verbatim into flow_check.py
reason: Most rules already exist; additions must be split into error versus warning severities rather than imported wholesale.
